sources.excerpt: EarthQuaker Devices Info Email Search Menu EarthQuaker Devices Info Email Search Devices Dealers Blog About Studios OnomatoPedal Merch "808-style" overdrive with 6 clipping voices, 5 bandwidth settings, 2 gain channels, switchable buffer, and boost. Palisades® Mega Ultimate Overdrive The Palisades is something we said we would never do… an overdrive based on the legendary TS808! After loads of requests, we finally buckled. We ran tests with every popular clone on the market as well as several vintage originals, compared, contrasted and took loads of notes. It was exhausting but informative. In the end, we threw it all away, used our ears and came up with what we feel is the most versatile relative of the 808 available today. With 6 different clipping voices, 5 bandwidth settings and 2 gain channels, you will be hard-pressed to not find a setting that will wipe every mid-boosting overdrive off your board. The Palisades is a versatile dude that will give you years of loving companionship. 1. Boost: Sets the level of the output boost. 2. Gain A: Sets the gain for the Channel A (lower gain) 3. Volume: Sets the output level. 4. Gain B: Sets the gain for Channel B (higher gain) 5. Tone: Brighter clockwise, warmer counterclockwise. Rotary Switches 6. Voice: This sets the nature of the Palisades distortion by changing the clipping diodes. No diodes: The most open and least distorted. LED clipping: Light clipping with a lot of volume. Mosfet clipping: Light gain OD with great harmonics. Asymmetrical Silicon clipping: Tighter light gain OD closest to stock 808. Symmetrical silicon clipping: Tighter distorted tone. Schottky Diode clipping: Looser fuzzy tone. 7. Bandwidth: This sets the overall tone and gain structure of the Palisades. 1 is the thinnest setting with the least amount of gain and 5 is the fattest setting with the heaviest gain. Everything else is in between. This control has a major effect on all the settings of the Palisades, especially the Gain and Voice controls. Toggle Switches 8. Normal/Bright: Normal is a warm full tone. Bright is livelier tone with more chime. 9. Buffer: Turns the input buffer on or off. ON is a tighter and brighter tone while OFF is a warmer tone with more sag. The buffer is part of the drive circuit & is only available when the Palisades is activated. Foot Switches 10. Boost: Activates the output level boost, Features Flexi-Switching. 11. Gain B: Activates Gain Channel B, Features Flexi-Switching. 12. Activate: True bypass switch GUITAR SAMPLES Gain A & B Gibson Les Paul

sources.title: EarthQuaker Palisades: The Biggest Tube Screamer Ever
sources.h1: EarthQuaker Devices Palisades: The Tube Screamer They Swore They Would Never Build
sources.excerpt: EarthQuaker Devices Palisades: 6 clipping voices, 5 bandwidths, 2 gain channels. History, V1 vs V2, verified players, tone recipes and buying advice. admin 22 September 2026 21 min read GG-ARTICLE-TOP Every boutique pedal company eventually builds a Tube Screamer. It is a rite of passage, like a bar band learning “Mustang Sally.” EarthQuaker Devices spent years insisting they were the exception — that the Akron workshop turning out fuzzes named after geological formations and doom-metal album titles had no interest in reheating the most cloned circuit in the history of the guitar. GG-ARTICLE-AFTER-INTRO Then, in May 2014, they gave in. And because it is EarthQuaker, they did not give in quietly. The Palisades arrived with five knobs, two rotary switches, two toggles, three footswitches and a subtitle — Mega Ultimate Overdrive — that reads less like a product name than a dare. Six clipping voices. Five bandwidth settings. Two independent gain channels. A separate boost. An input buffer you can switch out of the circuit entirely. Thirty distinct versions of the effect before you touch a single knob. EarthQuaker’s own launch copy did not pretend otherwise: “The Palisades is something we said we would never do… an overdrive based on the legendary TS808! After loads of requests, we finally buckled.” This is a feature, not a review. We are not handing out stars. We are here to explain what the Palisades actually is, what those thirty combinations really do, which players genuinely used one — and why a pedal this ambitious is now sitting on the discontinued list, hunted on the used market by people who should have bought one in 2019. How to Get the Tone ↓ Akron’s Anti-Tube-Screamer, And Why It Took Them Six Years EarthQuaker Devices’ origin story — Jamie Stillman, a basement in Akron, Ohio, a company built by a touring musician who got tired of touring — is told in full in our features on the EarthQuaker Devices Hoof Fuzz and the Acapulco Gold , so we will not repeat it here. What matters for the Palisades is the house philosophy that story produced: EarthQuaker built its reputation on pedals nobody else was making. Bit crushers. Octave-up monsters. Reverbs with a control literally labelled “Drag.” A one-knob distortion with no tone control at all. A Tube Screamer clone is the exact opposite of that. It is the safest, most crowded, most thoroughly solved corner of the pedal market. So when EarthQuaker finally entered it, the company’s stated method was almost comically thorough: “We ran tests with every popular clone on the market as well as several vintage originals, compared, contrasted and took loads of notes. It was exhausting but informative. In the end, we threw it all away, used our ears and came up with what we feel is the most versatile relative of the 808 available today.” That last phrase is the design brief in miniature. Not the most accurate relative of the 808. The most versatile . EarthQuaker’s answer to a saturated market was not to build a better copy but to build a machine that could be thirty copies at once — and then a dozen things a Tube Screamer has never been. The Palisades Timeline: 2014 To The Legacy Page 13 May 2014 — EarthQuaker announces the Palisades. It is publicly demoed at the 2014 Summer NAMM show in Nashville alongside three other new devices — the Afterneath reverb, the Cloven Hoof fuzz and the Arrows boost. Premier Guitar and Guitar World both file demo videos from the booth. US price: $249 . January 2016 — Trevor Curwen reviews the pedal for Guitarist and MusicRadar at £229/$249, and immediately reaches for the arithmetic: “ 30 variations on the character of the effect before you even start to tweak. “ October 2017 — Richard Purvis reviews it for Guitar Magazine (now Guitar.com) at £245, concluding that “ this box could replace three others. “ 4 December 2017 — EarthQuaker announces V2 . The Palisades is one of four pedals updated in the same batch, alongside the Arpanoid V2, the Grand Orbiter V3 and The Warden V2. Every one of them gets soft-touch, relay-based switching in place of the older hard-click mechanical footswitches, plus EarthQuaker’s Flexi-Switch behaviour: tap for standard latching, hold for momentary. UK RRP for the Palisades V2: £249 . Somewhere after that — the Dunes arrives: a compact, three-voice, two-bandwidth distillation of the Palisades in a standard-size enclosure, for players who wanted the sound without the real estate. As of 2026 — both are gone. EarthQuaker’s product pages for the Palisades and the Dunes now carry the same blunt line in capital letters: THIS DEVICE IS NO LONGER IN PRODUCTION. The Palisades survives only on the legacy list and the used market. The company’s current Tube-Screamer-adjacent offering is the far simpler, far cheaper Plumes . One small correction while we are on chronology: Equipboard’s spec table lists the Palisades’ production years as “2015 – 2017.” That understates it at both ends. The pedal was announced in May 2014 and V2 shipped from December 2017 onward, remaining in the catalogue for years afterward. Specifications Item Detail Model EarthQuaker Devices Palisades Mega Ultimate Overdrive Type “808-style” dual-channel overdrive with independent boost Announced 13 May 2014; demoed at Summer NAMM 2014, Nashville Launch price $249 US / £229–£249 UK Origin Hand-built in Akron, Ohio, USA Knobs Boost, Gain A, Volume, Gain B, Tone Rotary switches Voice (6 positions), Bandwidth (5 positions) Toggles Normal/Bright; Buffer On/Off Footswitches Activate (true bypass), Gain B, Boost Clipping voices 1. No diodes · 2. LED · 3. MOSFET · 4. Asymmetrical silicon · 5. Symmetrical silicon · 6. Schottky Switching V1: mechanical hard-click. V2: relay-based soft-touch with Flexi-Switch (latching + momentary) Dimensions 4.75 x 5.65 x 2.25 in (121 x 144 x 57 mm) with knobs Current draw 25 mA Input impedance 500 kΩ Output impedance <10 kΩ Power 9V DC only, 2.1 mm centre-negative.
